Dr Biodun Ogundipe has lauded the Supreme Court for affirming him as the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress in Ogun State for the 2027 election. Ogundipe, in a statement reacting to the judgment delivered by the apex court in Abuja on Tuesday, described the verdict as a landmark decision that reaffirmed the principles of truth, due process and strict adherence to established rules governing political party primaries. The Supreme Court had set aside the earlier decisions of the Federal High Court and the Court of Appeal, which had declared Otunba Jimi Lawal the ADC governorship candidate in Ogun State, thereby resolving the prolonged legal dispute in Ogundipe’s favour. Expressing appreciation to the judiciary, Ogundipe said the judgment had brought clarity to the controversy surrounding the party’s governorship primary and established the appropriate party organ with the authority to collate and declare election results. Ogundipe said, “I sincerely appreciate the Supreme Court of Nigeria for its landmark judgment affirming my candidacy as the duly recognised Gubernatorial Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Ogun State. “By setting aside the concurrent decisions of the Federal High Court and the Court of Appeal, which had declared Jimi Lawal as the party’s candidate, the apex court has reaffirmed the importance of truth, due process and strict adherence to the established rules governing political party primaries. According to him, the court’s recognition of the guidelines underscored the importance of respecting the constitutional and institutional structures through which political parties conduct their internal electoral processes. Ogundipe said, “I particularly commend the Supreme Court for recognising the clarity and organisational framework of the ADC’s Three-Tier Primary Election Guidelines established by the National Working Committee (NWC), in determining the conduct and outcome of the party’s primary election. “This decision is consistent with the Supreme Court’s established position on the constitutional and institutional powers of political parties in conducting their primary elections. I receive this judgment with humility, gratitude and a renewed sense of responsibility.” PHOTOS: Atiku promises to revive Ajaokuta steel plant, develop Idah port Yuletide: NAPTIP warns schoolchildren against antics of human traffickers 2027: Atiku promises cheaper fuel, stronger purchasing power He further thanked the ADC leadership, members, supporters and stakeholders for remaining steadfast throughout the legal contest, noting that their patience and confidence had sustained him during the period of uncertainty. Ogundipe urged party members to regard the judgment as an opportunity to strengthen internal unity and concentrate on positioning the ADC for the 2027 governorship election. He stressed that the time had come to move beyond the legal disagreement and work collectively towards the party’s political aspirations in Ogun State. “I thank the leadership of our great party, our supporters, stakeholders and members for their steadfastness, patience and confidence throughout this process. “The time has come to put the legal contest behind us, strengthen our party’s unity and focus collectively on the task ahead,” he said. In a unanimous judgment delivered on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, in Abuja, a five-member panel of the Supreme Court set aside the earlier decisions of the Federal High Court and the Court of Appeal, which had recognised Otunba Jimi Lawal as the party’s governorship candidate. The panel was presided over by Justice Emmanuel Akomaye Agim, while Justice Haruna Simon Tsammani read the lead judgment. The dispute arose from conflicting claims over the outcome of the ADC governorship primary election in the state. The disagreement culminated in a Federal High Court judgment in Abeokuta in July 2026, which overturned Ogundipe’s claim to the party’s ticket and declared Lawal the candidate. Dissatisfied with the ruling, Ogundipe challenged the decision, arguing that the party’s State Congress lacked the authority to collate and declare a result contrary to the outcome of the primary election conducted by the State Electoral Committee constituted by the party’s National Working Committee (NWC). The Supreme Court’s decision effectively restores Ogundipe’s claim to the ADC governorship ticket and settles the legal controversy over the party organ authorised to collate and declare the results of its primary elections. Taiwo Bankole
